glossary.definition: An electronic device that follows instructions to take in, process and output information.
glossary.example: A laptop is a computer you can carry and use for schoolwork.

glossary.definition: The physical parts of a computer you can see and touch.
glossary.example: The keyboard, mouse and screen are all examples of hardware.

glossary.definition: The instructions or programs that tell the hardware what to do.
glossary.example: A word processor and a game are both examples of software.

glossary.definition: A piece of hardware used to give information to the computer.
glossary.example: A keyboard and a mouse are input devices because they send data in.

glossary.definition: A piece of hardware that shows or gives out information from the computer.
glossary.example: A monitor and a printer are output devices because they show results.

glossary.definition: The screen of a computer that displays images and text.
glossary.example: She watched her essay on the monitor.

glossary.definition: A huge global network that connects computers so they can share information.
glossary.example: The internet lets you search for information and chat with friends far away.

glossary.definition: A program you use to look at and move around websites on the internet.
glossary.example: Chrome and Firefox are popular browsers.

glossary.definition: A way of sending and receiving messages over the internet, short for electronic mail.
glossary.example: She sent her homework to the teacher by e-mail.

glossary.definition: A named collection of information stored on a computer, like a document or picture.
glossary.example: He saved his drawing as a file called 'art.png'.

glossary.definition: A small portable device used to store and carry files between computers.
glossary.example: Take your project home on a USB flash drive.

glossary.definition: A software program used to create, edit and print text documents.
glossary.example: She used a word processor to type her letter.

glossary.definition: A personal computer designed to stay in one place on a desk or table.
glossary.example: The school computer lab has rows of desktop computers.

glossary.definition: A small, portable computer that can be folded shut and carried easily.
glossary.example: My father uses a laptop for his work at home.

glossary.definition: A flat, lightweight touchscreen computer that is larger than a smartphone.
glossary.example: She reads e-books on her tablet every evening.

glossary.definition: A handheld device that combines a mobile phone with computer features like internet access.
glossary.example: He uses his smartphone to check the weather forecast.

glossary.definition: An input device with keys used to type text and give commands to a computer.
glossary.example: She typed her essay using the keyboard.

glossary.definition: An input device moved by hand to control a pointer on the screen.
glossary.example: He clicked on the icon using the mouse.

glossary.definition: An output device that produces a paper copy of text or images from a computer.
glossary.example: The printer produced three copies of the class timetable.

glossary.definition: An input device that converts a paper document or photo into a digital image on the computer.
glossary.example: We used a scanner to save a copy of the photograph.

glossary.definition: An output device that produces sound from the computer.
glossary.example: We connected speakers to the computer to play music.

glossary.definition: An input device that captures sound and sends it to the computer.
glossary.example: The teacher used a microphone during the online lesson.

glossary.definition: A small camera that connects to a computer and is used for video calls and recording.
glossary.example: She used a webcam to join the video class from home.

glossary.definition: A display screen that you can touch with your finger to give commands.
glossary.example: Tablets and smartphones use a touchscreen instead of a mouse.

glossary.definition: An input device with a stick that can be moved in different directions to control action on the screen.
glossary.example: He used a joystick to control the plane in the flight game.

glossary.definition: An input device that uses a laser beam to read printed barcodes and convert them into data.
glossary.example: The shop assistant used a barcode reader to scan the price of the book.

glossary.definition: System software that manages the computer hardware and provides a platform for other programs to run.
glossary.example: Windows, macOS and Android are popular operating systems.

glossary.definition: Software designed to help the user perform specific tasks such as writing, calculating or browsing.
glossary.example: A word processor and a calculator are both types of application software.

glossary.definition: Software that controls and manages the basic operations of a computer hardware system.
glossary.example: Device drivers are a type of system software that let the operating system talk to the printer.

glossary.definition: Software designed to help analyse, configure, optimise or maintain a computer.
glossary.example: An antivirus program is a type of utility software that protects the computer from viruses.

glossary.definition: A set of written instructions and rules used to create software programs.
glossary.example: Python and JavaScript are programming languages used by developers.

glossary.definition: The process of changing the appearance of text in a document, such as font size, colour and alignment.
glossary.example: She used formatting to make the headings bold and centred.

glossary.definition: A built-in tool in word processors that finds and suggests corrections for misspelt words.
glossary.example: Spell check underlined the wrong word in red so she could fix it.

glossary.definition: A file created with a word processor that contains text and sometimes images.
glossary.example: He saved his science report as a document on the desktop.

glossary.definition: A software program used to organise, calculate and analyse numbers arranged in rows and columns.
glossary.example: The teacher used a spreadsheet to record our marks.

glossary.definition: The small box formed where a row and a column meet in a spreadsheet.
glossary.example: I typed the number 25 into cell B3.

glossary.definition: A mathematical expression in a spreadsheet that calculates a result from the data in other cells.
glossary.example: The formula =A1+B1 adds the values in cells A1 and B1.

glossary.definition: A horizontal line of cells in a spreadsheet, numbered from top to bottom.
glossary.example: Row 1 contains the column headings of the table.

glossary.definition: A vertical line of cells in a spreadsheet, labelled with letters from left to right.
glossary.example: Column A holds the names of all the students.

glossary.definition: A spreadsheet file that can contain one or more sheets for storing and organising data.
glossary.example: She created a workbook with separate sheets for each class.

glossary.definition: The web address of a page on the internet, short for Uniform Resource Locator.
glossary.example: Type the URL www.example.com into the browser to visit the site.

glossary.definition: A collection of related web pages that are stored on a server and accessed through the internet.
glossary.example: Our school has a website with news and photos.

glossary.definition: An online tool that helps you find information on the internet by searching for keywords.
glossary.example: Google is the most popular search engine in the world.

glossary.definition: The process of copying data from a remote computer or server to your own computer.
glossary.example: I will download the worksheet so I can read it offline.

glossary.definition: The process of sending data from your computer to a remote server or another computer over a network.
glossary.example: She uploaded her assignment to the school portal.

glossary.definition: A clickable link in a document or web page that takes you to another page or section when selected.
glossary.example: Click the hyperlink to open the video about the solar system.

glossary.definition: A wireless technology that lets devices connect to the internet without using cables.
glossary.example: Connect to the Wi-Fi to browse the internet on your phone.

glossary.definition: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over an internet connection in a given time.
glossary.example: A higher bandwidth means faster downloads and smoother video streaming.

glossary.definition: A communication tool that allows people to see and hear each other in real time over the internet.
glossary.example: We had a video call with our cousin in London.

glossary.definition: Websites and apps that allow people to create, share and exchange content and messages online.
glossary.example: Many people use social media to stay in touch with friends and family.

questions.question: Which of these is a computer?
questions.explanation: A laptop is a computer. The others are not computers.

questions.question: The physical parts of a computer that you can touch are called ___.
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical, touchable part of a computer like the keyboard and screen.

questions.question: Programs that tell the computer what to do are called ___.
questions.explanation: Software is the program or set of instructions that tells hardware what to do.

questions.question: Which of these is an INPUT device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard sends data into the computer, so it is an input device.

questions.question: Which of these is an OUTPUT device?
questions.explanation: A monitor shows information from the computer, so it is an output device.

questions.question: The screen of a computer that shows images and text is called a ___.
questions.explanation: The monitor is the display screen of the computer.

questions.question: The huge global network that connects computers to share information is the ___.
questions.explanation: The internet is the worldwide network that links computers together.

questions.question: Which program do you use to look at websites?
questions.explanation: A browser (like Chrome or Firefox) lets you view and navigate websites.

questions.question: Sending messages electronically over the internet is called ___.
questions.explanation: E-mail (electronic mail) is sending messages over the internet.

questions.question: A named collection of information stored on a computer, like a document, is a ___.
questions.explanation: A file is a named collection of data, such as a document or picture.

questions.question: Which device lets you carry files from one computer to another?
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive stores files so you can move them between computers.

questions.question: Software used to type and edit text documents is a ___.
questions.explanation: A word processor is software for creating and editing text documents.

questions.question: Which type of computer is designed to stay on a desk in one place?
questions.explanation: A desktop computer is designed to stay in one place on a desk or table.

questions.question: A small, portable computer that folds shut is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A laptop is a portable computer that can be folded shut and carried easily.

questions.question: A flat, lightweight computer with a touchscreen that is larger than a phone is a ___.
questions.explanation: A tablet is a flat touchscreen computer that is larger than a smartphone.

questions.question: Which device is both a mobile phone and a small computer?
questions.explanation: A smartphone combines a mobile phone with computer features like internet access.

questions.question: The input device with keys used to type text is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device with keys used to type text.

questions.question: Which input device do you move by hand to control the pointer on screen?
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device that controls the pointer on the screen.

questions.question: A file created with a word processor that contains text is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A document is a file created with a word processor that contains text.

questions.question: A horizontal line of cells in a spreadsheet is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A row is a horizontal line of cells numbered from top to bottom.

questions.question: A vertical line of cells in a spreadsheet labelled with letters is a ___.
questions.explanation: A column is a vertical line of cells labelled with letters from left to right.

questions.question: A collection of related web pages on the internet is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages stored on a server.

questions.question: Copying data from a server to your computer is called ___.
questions.explanation: Download means to copy data from a remote server to your own computer.

questions.question: Sending data from your computer to a server is called ___.
questions.explanation: Upload means to send data from your computer to a remote server.

questions.question: A computer can only process numbers, not text.
questions.explanation: A computer can process both numbers and text, as well as images, sound and video.

questions.question: A mouse is an example of computer hardware.
questions.explanation: A mouse is a physical part of a computer system, so it is hardware.

questions.question: What does a monitor do?
questions.explanation: A monitor is the screen that displays images and text from the computer.

questions.question: The internet is a network that only exists in Ghana.
questions.explanation: The internet is a global network that connects computers all around the world.

questions.question: Which of these pairs are both INPUT devices?
questions.explanation: Both the mouse and keyboard send data into the computer, so they are input devices.

questions.question: Which of these pairs are both OUTPUT devices?
questions.explanation: Speakers produce sound and printers produce paper copies, so both are output devices.

questions.question: A browser is a hardware device used to type documents.
questions.explanation: A browser is a software program used to view and navigate websites, not a hardware device.

questions.question: E-mail stands for electronic mail.
questions.explanation: E-mail is short for electronic mail, a way of sending messages over the internet.

questions.question: A folder is the same thing as a file.
questions.explanation: A folder is a container that holds files, while a file is a single unit of stored information.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a USB flash drive?
options: It is small and portable for carrying files
It displays images on a screen
It connects to the internet wirelessly
questions.correctAnswer: It is small and portable for carrying files
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive is small and portable, making it easy to carry files between computers.

questions.question: A word processor can only type plain text with no formatting.
questions.explanation: A word processor supports formatting such as bold, italic, font changes and alignment.

questions.question: A printer is which type of device?
questions.explanation: A printer gives out information from the computer onto paper, so it is an output device.

questions.question: What does a scanner do?
options: Converts a paper document into a digital image
questions.correctAnswer: Converts a paper document into a digital image
questions.explanation: A scanner reads a paper document or photo and converts it into a digital image on the computer.

questions.question: Which device produces sound from a computer?
questions.explanation: A speaker is an output device that produces sound from the computer.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of an operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system that manages computer hardware and software.

questions.question: A word processor and a web browser are examples of ___.
questions.explanation: Application software helps users perform specific tasks such as writing or browsing.

questions.question: Changing the font size, colour and alignment of text is called ___.
questions.explanation: Formatting is the process of changing the appearance of text such as font size and alignment.

questions.question: Which tool in a word processor finds and corrects misspelt words?
questions.explanation: Spell check is a built-in tool that finds and suggests corrections for misspelt words.

questions.question: A spreadsheet is used to ___.
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet organises, calculates and analyses numbers arranged in rows and columns.

questions.question: The web address you type into a browser is called a ___.
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator and is the address of a web page.

questions.question: Which tool helps you find information on the internet by searching keywords?
questions.explanation: A search engine like Google helps you find information on the internet using keywords.

questions.question: In a supermarket, the device used to scan the price label on a product is a ___.
questions.explanation: A barcode reader uses a laser beam to read the printed barcode and convert it into price data.

questions.question: Which type of software controls the basic operations of computer hardware and lets other programs run?
questions.explanation: System software controls the basic operations of computer hardware and provides a platform for other programs.

questions.question: An antivirus program is an example of which type of software?
questions.explanation: Utility software helps maintain and protect a computer, and antivirus is a type of utility software.

questions.question: Which of these is a programming language?
questions.explanation: Python is a programming language used by developers to write software programs.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, a formula that adds the values in cells A1 and A2 is written as ___.
questions.explanation: In a spreadsheet, formulas start with an equals sign, so it is written as =A1+A2.

questions.question: A spreadsheet file that can contain one or more sheets is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A workbook is a spreadsheet file that can contain one or more sheets for organising data.

questions.question: A clickable link on a web page that takes you to another page is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a clickable link that navigates you to another page or section.

questions.question: The maximum amount of data that can be sent over an internet connection in a given time is called ___.
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum data that can be transmitted over a connection in a given time.

questions.question: Software that manages computer hardware and provides a platform for programs is the ___.
questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware and provides a platform for application software to run.

questions.question: System software and application software are both types of software.
questions.explanation: Both system software and application software are categories of software that run on a computer.

questions.question: In a spreadsheet, cell C4 is found at the intersection of ___.
options: Both B and C are correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both B and C are correct
questions.explanation: Cell C4 is where column C and row 4 meet, which is the same as row 4 and column C.

questions.question: Which input device captures sound and sends it to the computer?
questions.explanation: A microphone is an input device that captures sound and converts it into a digital signal for the computer.

questions.question: Which feature allows a user to give commands by touching the screen directly?
questions.explanation: A touchscreen is a display that responds to touch, allowing users to give commands with their fingers.

questions.question: A device with a stick that can be moved in different directions to control games is a ___.
questions.explanation: A joystick is an input device with a movable stick used to control action in games and simulations.

questions.question: Which communication tool allows people to see and hear each other in real time over the internet?
questions.explanation: A video call allows people to see and hear each other in real time using a webcam and internet connection.
